annotations.annotation_text: Page 552 opens Book 3, Chapter 3 ("The Inquest of Yawn") during the Age of Men phase. This passage continues the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession, featuring Yawn/Shaun, Mamalujo, HCE (voice), ALP (voice). The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/annotationstofin0000mchu_h5g8
Gordon, John. Finnegans Wake: A Plot Summary. https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com
JJDA: Finnegans Wake Genetic Edition. https://jjda.ie

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 552 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Men dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
Contemporary Literature Press: Multilingual Lexicons for FW. https://editura.mttlc.ro
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe

annotations.annotation_text: Fall/resurrection motif "wall" on page 552 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): Tim Finnegan tumbling from his ladder, Humpty Dumpty shattering from the wall, Adam falling in Eden — all converge within the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession. The comic-cosmic Fall during the Age of Men phase demands its counterpart: resurrection through the whiskey-splash of the water of life (uisce beatha).
sources: The Ballad of Tim Finnegan's Wake. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnegan%27s_Wake
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Opie, Iona and Peter. The Oxford Dictionary of Nursery Rhymes. https://archive.org/details/oxforddictionary0000unse_m4u1
